sara: Heads up — trying to onboard a HF chat model into Redwood and hitting weird tool-calling/JSON mode tokenization problems. After conversion the model strips our <json> markers and tool tags sometimes, causing parser errors in downstream evals. anyone seen this? :thinking:

kai: Can you paste the tokenizer config you used when converting? Often special_tokens_map or additional_special_tokens get lost.

sara: Sure, here's what I passed to transformers before export:
```json
{
  "bos_token": "<s>",
  "eos_token": "</s>",
  "additional_special_tokens": ["<tool>", "</tool>", "<json>", "</json>", "<|role|user|>", "<|role|assistant|>"]
}
```
But after Redwood conversion the model emits tokens like "<|role|user|>" as multiple subwords and sometimes the tokenizer decoder drops angle brackets. The JSON-mode detector in our client fails.

olga: Did you check tokenizer.add_special_tokens after loading into Redwood runtime? Some conversion paths expect tokens in the config.json but also in the tokenizer files (merges/vocab) — mismatch causes fallback to default unknown tokenization.

sara: I called hf_to_redwood.convert_model(...) which copies config.json, merges, vocab. The artifact shows the config had the specials but tokenizer.json in the converted bundle lacks them.

mike: We saw a similar issue during quantization experiments. When we quantified to int8, the reduced-precision kernels influenced cache alignment and the runtime's decode path did a round-trip that normalized unicode/angle-bracket tokens. Not sure if that's related but it's a red flag. :eyes:

kai: Two-pronged checklist:
- Ensure additional_special_tokens written into tokenizer.json and tokenizer.config — not only model config.json.
- For chat templates, persist role markers as single-token entries (e.g., <role_user>) instead of pipes/vertical bars that tokenizers split.
- Set tokenizer.add_prefix_space = True for byte-level BPE variants so markers don't attach to previous token.

sara: Good call. I can try normalizing role tokens to single-token forms. But we really need to keep the original markers in evals to avoid changing prompt semantics. Any ideas for preserving both forms?

olga: One hack: keep both variants as specials, e.g. additional_special_tokens includes "<|role|user|>", "<role_user>" and add a small preprocessor that maps incoming strings to the canonical single-token form before tokenization. That keeps backward compatibility with saved prompts.

kai: Also watch out for JSON-mode markers like <json> and </json>. If tokenizer strips them at decode time, the model still generated the tokens but the client-side decode step removes them — we had to set skip_special_tokens=False in the Redwood runtime decode path to surface them. Are you controlling decode kwargs?

sara: Right now decode uses default settings in the deploy config. Where do we set skip_special_tokens on Redwood?

mike: In the model route config: set decoder_options: { "skip_special_tokens": false } or use the per-request parameter. For Dedicated/Private you can also patch the runtime's tokenizer wrapper to expose decode options globally.

sara: Nice. That helps the JSON markers, but there's another problem: our tool-calling schema uses a custom tool tag syntax of the form <<TOOL:name|json>> ... <</TOOL>> — these pipes and angle combos get tokenized into multiple tokens and sometimes quantized logits favor boundary tokens so the model emits only closing tag. Leads to malformed JSON inside tools.

olga: For tool-calling we recommend switching to ASCII-safe single-token wrappers, e.g. _TOOL_START_name_ and _TOOL_END_. Ugly but reliable across tokenizers and quantization regimes. Also add them as additional_special_tokens so they are single tokens.

sara: We're trying to avoid changing the wire format used by clients. If we can't change tags, maybe make postprocessing more tolerant? e.g. fuzzy repair heuristics for JSON and tag balancing.

kai: Add fallback policies: if canonical tags not present, try to reconstruct by scanning for partial tag tokens and re-assembling. Also add an eval that computes "tag fidelity" — fraction of responses that have intact start/end tool tags. Run it across float32 vs int8 vs int4 quantized variants.

mike: To reproduce locally: export HF model -> convert -> run Redwood local runtime with logging enabled: set LOG_TOKEN_SPANS=1 to get token->string mapping in logs. Then diff tokens emitted vs tokens decoded. That helped us spot the token-split issue quickly.

sara: Thanks — I'll run the LOG_TOKEN_SPANS flow and add both tokenizers entries to the converted package. One more Q: config.json role token names vs chat template placeholders — sometimes chat template uses <|user|> but model config uses <role_user>. Is that a problem?

olga: Yes. Chat template placeholders must match tokenizer special tokens; otherwise the template engine will inject raw text that gets tokenized differently. We ended up normalizing templates at conversion time: map placeholders to the tokenizer's canonical special token. Build a small mapping table in the conversion script.

sara: Ok plan: 1) patch conversion to ensure additional_special_tokens copied into tokenizer.json and tokenizers config, 2) add canonical single-token fallbacks for problematic markers, 3) enable skip_special_tokens=false in decode for eval runs, 4) run quantization fidelity sweep (fp32 vs int8 vs int4) and compute tag fidelity metric. I'll post results here. :+1:
